name: export-dashboard
title: Excel dashboard
description: Excel project controls dashboard of a P6 project (one A3 page and detail sheets), then a short summary of its cards, counts, failed DCMA checks and warnings (the database is never written). Use when the user asks for an Excel dashboard or a one-page project report.

args.name: project
args.description: Project ID as shown in P6

args.name: path
args.description: Full path of the .xlsx file to write

args.name: baseline
args.description: Project ID of the baseline (empty = the project baseline)

args.name: prepared_by
args.description: Name printed under the title (may be empty)

args.name: revision
args.description: Revision printed under the title (may be empty)

args.name: company
args.description: Company name in the sidebar (may be empty)

args.name: colors
args.description: Colors 'primary,accent' in hex, for example 1F3864,C00000 (may be empty)

template:
Excel project controls dashboard of project {project}, written to {path}, then a short summary of its cards, counts, failed DCMA checks and warnings. The P6 database is never written.

This skill gives you every figure: you copy fields, you never compute them.
- reference/spec.json: the calls, the slots (each a field of one call) and the tables.
- reference/fields.md: for every slot and table column, its field, unit, format and meaning.
- reference/report.md: the report to fill.
- reference/checks.md: stop rules and checks to run before answering.
- reference/example.md: the report filled on a demo project (an example of the format, not of the figures).

Calls, in this order:
1. sum = p6_project_summary(project="{project}", baseline="{baseline}"): data date, last F9, schedule state and the baseline used, before the file is written.
2. dash = p6_export_dashboard(project="{project}", path="{path}", baseline="{baseline}", prepared_by="{prepared_by}", revision="{revision}", company="{company}", colors="{colors}"): writes the workbook (never the database): the 7 cards as written, counts, failed DCMA checks, warnings.
Leave out an argument whose value is empty (baseline, colors, company, prepared_by, revision).

Between the two calls and around call 2:
- After call 1, if sum.schedule_state.stale is true or edited_since_last_schedule is not null, say so and
  ask the user whether to export anyway or to press F9 in P6 first; wait for the answer. If
  sum.baseline.used is null, say that the delayed count, the variance cards and the baseline bars will
  stay empty.
- If a file already exists at <path>, call 2 is refused: ask the user whether to replace it, and only on
  a yes repeat call 2 with the same arguments and overwrite=true.
- If the file is open in Excel, call 2 is refused: ask the user to close it, then run call 2 again.

Write the report:
1. Start from reference/report.md. Replace each slot placeholder (a slot name in curly braces) by the field
   named in spec.json slots (call and path), written in the slot's format (reference/fields.md). An argument
   written <name> in these instructions is the placeholder of that name in curly braces in report.md and
   checks.md: the value given (an empty optional argument is left out of the calls).
2. Replace each line [table: name] by that table: one row per item of its list, in the order returned, at
   most its cap, every cell in its column's format, the heads as in spec.json. A table with a totals entry
   ends with its Total row, taken from the totals of its call, never from adding the rows. Only a table
   built from the rows list of its call ends, when that call has more pages (next_offset not null), with
   the line "Showing the first <returned> of <total> <noun>." (returned and total of that call). A table
   built from another list or dict of the call (weeks, paths, roots, causes, counts...) ends with "Only the
   first <cap> <noun> are shown." when that list is longer than the cap, and never with a Showing line. An
   empty list gives the table's empty text; a call that failed or was skipped gives no table.
3. Keep the lines between [if: slot] and [end if] only when the slot is true (true, a number other than 0,
   a text or list that is not empty, an ID - name whose ID is not null), the lines between [if not: slot]
   and [end if] only when it is not; remove the markers.
4. Numbers: take the number as written in the result and round it, halves away from zero, to the decimals
   of its format (-104274.95 in n1 is -104,275.0); whole numbers and counts take a comma between thousands
   (1,227), also in the Showing lines. A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text, and so
   is an ID - name whose ID is null.
5. Never add, subtract, divide, count rows or match rows of two results: a figure that is not a slot or a
   table cell is left out. Ignore the note fields of the tools unless a slot names them.
6. Write the headings and sentences in the user's language; keep values, IDs, names and number formats
   exactly as formatted.
7. Run reference/checks.md before answering. Report a failed cross-check, never hide it; say nothing about
   the checks that pass.

For this skill:
- The card values (their text) and details are copied as returned; a | inside a cell is written /.
- File paths are written exactly as returned.

files.text:
# Excel dashboard of {project}

File written: {file}. The P6 database was not changed.

Data date {data_date}, last schedule run (F9) {last_f9}. Baseline: {bl_used}.

[if: stale]
Warning: this project was changed after its last F9. The dashboard shows the dates, float and critical path of the last F9: open P6, press F9, then export again.
[end if]

[if not: bl_used]
No baseline: the delayed activities card, the variance cards and the baseline bars stay empty. Set a project baseline in P6 or pass baseline= to fill them.
[end if]

## Cards (as written on the Dashboard)

[table: cards]

## Contents

- Activities: {n_acts}; WBS nodes: {n_wbs}; milestones: {n_ms}; critical activities: {n_crit}.

## DCMA checks that fail

[table: dcma_failed]

## Warnings

[table: warnings]

## How to use the file

- The Dashboard sheet prints on one A3 landscape page and is protected without a password.
- The Schedule Overview opens folded to WBS level 2: the outline buttons on the left unfold it.
- The Critical Path sheet lists the P6 float paths of the last F9 (when P6 stored none, the near critical activities grouped by total float).
- Every figure comes from the last F9: after changes in P6, press F9 and export again.

# Checks before answering

## Stop rules (write the sentence, then stop)

- A call says the project is not found: "Project <project> was not found: check the Project ID (p6_list_projects)."
- p6_project_summary says the baseline is not found: repeat its message and stop.
- Before call 2, sum.schedule_state.stale is true or edited_since_last_schedule is not null: "The schedule of
  <project> was changed after its last F9: export anyway, or press F9 in P6 first?" Wait for the answer.
- p6_export_dashboard says the file already exists: "<path> already exists: replace it?" Only after the
  user's yes, run call 2 again with the same arguments and overwrite=true. Never pass overwrite=true
  without that yes.
- p6_export_dashboard says it cannot write the file (open in Excel): "Close <path> in Excel, then tell me
  to export again." Run call 2 again only when the user says so.
- p6_export_dashboard says the schedule changed during the export: run call 2 again once; if it fails
  again, repeat its message and stop.
- Any other error of call 2 (path not .xlsx, folder missing, bad colors): repeat its message and stop.

## Cross-checks (each pair must be equal)

1. sum.schedule_state.data_date = dash.data_date (same data date).
2. sum.schedule_state.last_schedule_date = dash.schedule_state.last_schedule_date (same last F9).
3. sum.baseline.used = dash.baseline (same baseline).
4. sum.activities.total = dash.counts.activities.
5. sum.counts.wbs = dash.counts.wbs.
6. sum.critical.critical = dash.counts.critical.

If a pair differs, the database changed between the calls: say which pair differs and ask the user to
export again once the F9 in P6 is done.

## Before sending

- Every number, date and count is a slot or a table cell of reference/fields.md, copied from its field
  and written in its format. Nothing was added, subtracted, divided, counted or matched by you.
- The cards table has the 7 cards of dash.cards in their order: the text (the value as Excel shows it) and the
  detail as returned, a | inside a detail written /.
- The DCMA checks are dash.dcma_failed in their order; its empty text when the list is empty.
- Every warning of dash.warnings is listed.
- The stale and no baseline blocks are kept only when their slot says so.
- Headings and sentences are in the user's language; values, IDs, names, file paths and number formats
  exactly as formatted.

# Fields of Excel dashboard

Generated from reference/spec.json by the catalog build. Each slot of reference/report.md is copied from one field of one call; write it in its format, never compute it.

## Calls

1. sum = p6_project_summary(project="{project}", baseline="{baseline}"): data date, last F9, schedule state and the baseline used, before the file is written.
2. dash = p6_export_dashboard(project="{project}", path="{path}", baseline="{baseline}", prepared_by="{prepared_by}", revision="{revision}", company="{company}", colors="{colors}"): writes the workbook (never the database): the 7 cards as written, counts, failed DCMA checks, warnings.
Leave out an argument whose value is empty (baseline, colors, company, prepared_by, revision).

## Formats

- text: the value as returned
- int: the whole number, a comma between thousands: 1,227
- date: the first 10 characters: YYYY-MM-DD
- datetime: the first 16 characters: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
- n0: the number as written in the result rounded to a whole number, halves away from zero, a comma between thousands: 12,345
- n1: the same to 1 decimal: 12,345.6 (-104274.95 gives -104,275.0)
- n2: the same to 2 decimals: 12,345.67
- pct1: the same to 1 decimal, then %: 49.7%
- flag: yes for true, no for false
- id_name: the two fields joined: ID - Name (the ID alone when the name is null, the none text when the ID is null)
- list: the items of the list in their order, joined by a comma and a space: in_progress, finishing
- A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text (n/a unless stated).
- [if: slot] is true for true, a number other than 0, a text or list that is not empty.

## Arguments

- {project}: Project ID as shown in P6, as given
- {path}: Full path of the .xlsx file to write, as given
- {baseline}: Project ID of the baseline (empty = the project baseline), as given
- {prepared_by}: Name printed under the title (may be empty), as given
- {revision}: Revision printed under the title (may be empty), as given
- {company}: Company name in the sidebar (may be empty), as given
- {colors}: Colors 'primary,accent' in hex, for example 1F3864,C00000 (may be empty), as given

## Units

- count: a count

## Slots

| Slot | Field (call.path) | Unit | Format | None | Meaning |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| data_date | sum.schedule_state.data_date |  | date | n/a | data date of the project |
| last_f9 | sum.schedule_state.last_schedule_date |  | datetime | n/a | last schedule run (F9) in P6 |
| stale | sum.schedule_state.stale |  | flag | n/a | this server changed the project after the last F9 |
| bl_used | sum.baseline.used |  | text | none | Project ID of the baseline used (baseline= else the project baseline) |
| file | dash.path |  | text | n/a | the .xlsx file written |
| n_acts | dash.counts.activities | count | int | n/a | activities in the Schedule Overview |
| n_wbs | dash.counts.wbs | count | int | n/a | WBS nodes, the project node included |
| n_ms | dash.counts.milestones | count | int | n/a | milestones in the Dashboard table (at most 30) |
| n_crit | dash.counts.critical | count | int | n/a | critical open activities under the project's definition |

## Table cards

The 7 cards of the Dashboard sheet in their order, value (as Excel shows it) and detail as written.

Rows: dash.cards, in the order returned, at most 7 (a dict gives one row per item: its key is _key, a plain value _value).
When the list holds more than 7 items, add the line: Only the first 7 cards are shown.
No rows: write 'No card written.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Card | card |  | text | n/a |  |
| Value | text |  | text | n/a |  |
| Detail | detail |  | text | n/a |  |

## Table dcma_failed

DCMA 14 checks whose pass is false, in DCMA order (tool names).

Rows: dash.dcma_failed, in the order returned, at most 15 (a dict gives one row per item: its key is _key, a plain value _value).
When the list holds more than 15 items, add the line: Only the first 15 checks are shown.
No rows: write 'Every DCMA check with a threshold passes.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Failed check | (the row itself) |  | text | n/a |  |

## Table warnings

Warnings of the export, as returned.

Rows: dash.warnings, in the order returned, at most 20 (a dict gives one row per item: its key is _key, a plain value _value).
When the list holds more than 20 items, add the line: Only the first 20 warnings are shown.
No rows: write 'No warning.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Warning | (the row itself) |  | text | n/a |  |

## Cross-checks (equal values)

- same data date in the summary and the export: sum.schedule_state.data_date = dash.data_date
- same last F9 in the summary and the export: sum.schedule_state.last_schedule_date = dash.schedule_state.last_schedule_date
- same baseline in the summary and the export: sum.baseline.used = dash.baseline
- same number of activities: sum.activities.total = dash.counts.activities
- same number of WBS nodes: sum.counts.wbs = dash.counts.wbs
- same critical count: sum.critical.critical = dash.counts.critical

File written: C:\P6\demo\DEMO-SS225.xlsx. The P6 database was not changed.

Data date 2026-10-26, last schedule run (F9) 2026-10-26 17:30. Baseline: DEMO-SS225_BL.

| Card | Value | Detail |
|-|-|-|
| Overall Progress | 49.67% | Planned: 54.06%  /  Variance: -4.40% |

## How to use the file

- The Schedule Overview opens folded to WBS level 2: the outline buttons on the left unfold it.
- The Critical Path sheet lists the P6 float paths of the last F9 (when P6 stored none, the near critical activities grouped by total float).
- Every figure comes from the last F9: after changes in P6, press F9 and export again.
